==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|weake||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|waik}}, {{m|enm|wayk}}, {{m|enm|wayke}}, {{m|enm|weik}}, {{m|enm|weyk}}, borrowed from {{der|en|non|veikr|t=weak}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*waikwaz|t=weak, yielded, pliant, bendsome}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*wīkwaną|t=to cease, fold, yield; to retreat}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*weyg-|t=to bend, turn, wind}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*weh₁y-|t=to plait, twist, weave, wind; to cover, enclose, wrap}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|ang|wāc|t=bendsome, weak}}, {{cog|stq|wook|t=soft, gentle, tender}}, {{cog|fy|weak|t=soft}}, {{cog|nl|week|t=soft, weak}}, {{cog|de|weich|t=soft, weak}}, {{cog|lb|weech|t=weak}}, {{cog|yi|ווייך|t=soft}}, {{cog|da|veg|t=weak}}, {{cog|fo,is|veikur|t=weak}}, {{cog|nb|veik}}, {{m|nb|vek|t=weak; pliant}}, {{cog|nn|veik|t=weak}}, {{cog|sv|vek|t=weak, pliant}}, {{cog|et|vaik}}, {{m|et|vaikne|t=quiet}}, {{cog|fi|vaieta|t=to fall silent; to be silent; to keep silent; to suppress by not discussing}}, {{cog|izh|vaiketa|t=quiet down}}; also {{cog|kw|gwigh|t=winkles}}, {{cog|ga|faocha}}, {{m|ga|faochóg|t=periwinkle}}, {{cog|la|vicis|t=change; time; season; succession; lot; place, room, stead}}, {{m|la|vieo|t=to bend}}, {{cog|grc|οἴγω|t=to open}}, {{cog|sq|vig|t=bier, litter, stretcher}}, {{cog|lt|vyti|t=to twist, wind}}, {{cog|be|віць|t=to twist, weave}}, {{cog|bg|ви́я|t=to bend, twist; to roam; to swirl}}, {{cog|cs|vít|t=to weave, wind; to wrap}}, {{cog|pl,hsb|wić|t=to plait, weave; to wriggle, writhe}}, {{cog|ru|вить|t=to wind; to twist, weave}}, {{cog|sh|ви̏ти}}, {{m|sh|vȉti|t=to twist}}, {{cog|sl|viti|t=to twist}}, {{cog|uk|ви́ти|t=to twist, wind; to plait; to build a nest; to curl}}, {{cog|kmr|avêtin}}, {{m|kmr|avitin}}, {{m|kmr|avîtin}}, {{m|kmr|havêtin}}, {{m|kmr|havîtin|t=to cast, throw}}, {{cog|fa|آویختن|tr=âvixtan|t=to hang, suspend}}, {{m|fa|بیختن|tr=bēxtan / bixtan|t=to sift}}, {{cog|sa|वेग|t=speed, impetus; stream; agitation; impetuosity; strength; haste; the flight of an arrow; love; delight; expulsion; semen; attack; constipation}}. 
{{col-bottom}}
Related to {{cog|ang|wīcan|t=to yield}}. Related to {{doublet|en|week|wick<id:corner>|nocat=1|notext=1}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline|weak}}</ref>

The grammar sense is a {{clq|en|de|schwach|nocap=1}}.

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|er}}

# Lacking in [[force]] (usually strength) or [[ability]].
#: {{ux|en|The child was too '''weak''' to move the boulder.}}
#: {{ux|en|This is not a job for someone with a '''weak''' stomach.}}
#: {{ux|en|They easily guessed his '''weak''' computer password.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare King Lear|act=III|scene=ii|passage=a poor, infirm, '''weak''', and despised old man}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|Palamon and Arcite
|passage='''weak''' with hunger, mad with love}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Julia Horowitz|title=‘The worst is yet to come’: IMF issues stark recession warning|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/10/11/economy/imf-world-economic-outlook/index.html|date=2022-10-11|passage=The prospects for the global economy as outlined by the IMF are the third '''weakest''' since 2001, behind only the 2008 financial crisis and the worst phase of the coronavirus pandemic. Global growth has fallen below 2% just five times since 1970.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805051832/https://www.cnn.com/2022/10/11/economy/imf-world-economic-outlook/index.html}}
# Unable to sustain a great weight, pressure, or strain.
#: {{ux|en|a '''weak''' timber; a '''weak''' rope}}
# {{U|limp}}, [[soft]].
# Unable to withstand temptation, urgency, persuasion, etc.; easily impressed, moved, or overcome; accessible; vulnerable.
#: {{ux|en|'''weak''' resolutions; '''weak''' virtue}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1703|author=w:Nicholas Rowe|title=The Fair Penitent|section=act I, scene I
|passage=Guard thy heart / On this '''weak''' side, where most our nature fails.}}
# {{lb|en|''often with'' for}} Having a strong, irrepressible emotional love for someone or (less often) something; sentimentally affected by such love.
# [[dilute|Dilute]], lacking in [[taste]] or [[potency]].
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=2|passage=''That'' the young Mr. Churchills liked—but they did not like him coming round of an evening and drinking '''weak''' whisky-and-water while he held forth on railway debentures and corporation loans. Mr. Barrett, however, by fawning and flattery, seemed to be able to make not only Mrs. Churchill but everyone else do what he desired.}}
#: {{ux|en|We were served stale bread and '''weak''' tea.}}
# {{lb|en|grammar}}{{wikipedia|Weak inflection}} Displaying a particular kind of [[inflection]], including:
#: {{ant|en|strong}}
## {{lb|en|{{w|Germanic languages}}|of|{{lg|verb}}s}} [[regular|Regular]] in [[inflection]], lacking vowel changes and having a past tense marked by /-d-/, /-t-/, or /-ð-/.
##: {{cot|en|strong|irregular}}
##: {{ux|en|The verb ''to walk'' is '''weak''' because it has a past tense of ''walked'' and all forms are inflected by adding the typical suffix (ie is regular) to the stem ''walk-'' (ie has no vowel changes). }}
##: {{ux|en|The verb ''to run'' is strong, not '''weak''', because the past tense is ''ran''.}}
##: {{ux|en|The verb ''to be'' is neither '''weak''' nor strong, instead it is highly irregular in all inflections; its third person present tense is ''is'' instead of ''*bes'' (which can even be seen in this very sentence) and its past tense is ''was'' or ''were'' instead of ''*bed'' or ''*beed'' or anything similar, just to name a few of its inflections.}}
## {{lb|en|Germanic languages|of|{{lg|noun}}s}} Showing less distinct grammatical endings.
## {{lb|en|Germanic languages|of|{{lg|adjective}}s}} [[definite|Definite]] in meaning, often used with a definite article or similar word.
## {{lb|en|{{w|Semitic languages}}}} Related to, containing, or being a consonant which is prone to disappearing in some inflections, in most<!--all?--> applicable languages including (but not limited to) w and y.
##: {{ux|en|In some Semitic languages such as Akkadian, some or all gutturals are '''weak''' and often disappear, but in others such as Arabic and Ugaritic, they are strong and never disappear.}}
##: {{ux|en|The reflexes of the {{w|Proto-Semitic}} verb {{m|sem-pro|*mawut-|t=to die}} are often '''weak''' due to the presence of ''w'', for example: {{m+|ar|مَاتَ}}, {{m+|he|מֵת|tr=mēṯ}}, and {{m+|uga|𐎎𐎚|ts=māta}}.}}
## {{lb|en|{{w|Uralic languages}}}} Related to, being, or containing the [[lenis]] [[consonant gradation]], which resulted from historically closed syllables.
##: {{ux|en|The {{w|Finnish language|Finnish}} verb {{m|fi|kääntää|t=to translate}} inflects to the singular imperative as {{m|fi||käännä}}, showing the '''weak''' gradation ''nt > nn'' because it historically ended in a consonant which closed the syllable.}}
# {{lb|en|Indo-European studies|especially of {{lg|stem}}s or inflected {{lg|root}}s}} Of a form in which the [[accent]] tends to shift [[forwards]] (to the right, in transcription) or did so ancestrally in [[Proto-Indo-European]], relative to the [[strong]] stem (which has the leftmost accent allowed).
#: {{ant|en|strong}}
#: {{ux|en|The [[PIE]] {{lg|zero grade}} was most often found in '''weak''' stems, such as in {{m|ine-pro||*mn̥téys|of thought, from thinking|pos=genitive/ablative singular of {{m|ine-pro|*méntis}}}} and {{m|ine-pro|*mn̥yétor|*mn̥yóh₂er|I am thinking}}. Over time it spread to strong stems, i.e. {{m|ine-pro||*mń̥tis}}, by processes of analogy and leveling. The {{lg|full grade}} was persistent in the first syllable of [[reduplicated]] [[stative]] verbs: strong {{m|ine-pro|*tetórpe|*tetórph₂e|I am satisfied}}, '''weak''' {{m|ine-pro||*tetr̥pmé|we all are satisfied}}, though for some verbs such as {{m|ine-pro|*píph₃eti|*pí-ph₃-e-|to drink}} there was an unusual ''i''-grade which may have lacked any distinct '''weak''' counterpart.}}
## {{lb|en|of {{lg|noun}}s and {{lg|adjective}}s}} In a [[grammatical case]] other than [[nominative]], [[accusative]], [[vocative]] or sometimes [[locative]] [[singular]].
## {{lb|en|of {{lg|verb}}s}} In a [[conjugation]] other than [[singular]] [[active]] forms (regardless of [[person]], [[tense]] etc.).
##: {{ux|en|All [[middle]] forms of Indo-European verbs are traditionally '''weak'''. Middle-only verbs can still be compared to hypothetical strong stems, such as '''weak''' {{m|ine-pro||*ǵn̥h₁-yé-}} (e.g. {{m|ine-pro|*ǵn̥h₁yétor|*ǵn̥h₁yéto}}, {{m-g|(he/she/it) was born}}) versus strong {{m|ine-pro||*ǵénh₁-ye-}}.}}
# {{lb|en|phonology}} [[lenis|Lenis]], pronounced with less force or less [[markedness]].
# {{lb|en|chemistry}} That does not [[ionize]] completely into [[anion]]s and [[cation]]s in a [[solution]].
#: {{coi|en|a '''weak''' acid}};  {{coi|en|a '''weak''' base}}
#: {{ux|en|When we say that an acid is '''weak''', we refer only to its degree of dissociation, not to its degree of corrosiveness; but it is true that those two traits often correlate, though.<!--An exception is [[hydrofluoric acid]].-->}}
# {{lb|en|physics}} One of the four [[fundamental]] [[force]]s associated with [[nuclear]] [[decay]].
# {{lb|en|slang}} [[bad|Bad]] or [[uncool]].
#: {{ux|en|This place is '''weak'''.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|logic}} Having a narrow range of logical consequences; narrowly applicable. (Often contrasted with a {{l|en|strong}} statement which implies it.)
# Resulting from, or indicating, lack of judgment, discernment, or firmness; unwise; hence, foolish.
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=9|passage=If evil thence ensue, / She first his '''weak''' indulgence will accuse.|year=1873}}
# Not having power to convince; not supported by force of reason or truth; unsustained.
#: {{ux|en|The prosecution advanced a '''weak''' case.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|book=3|passage=convinced of his '''weak''' arguing}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Joseph L. Taylor|title=Foundations of Analysis|publisher=w:American Mathematical Society|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=0ky2W1loV-QC&pg=PA114&dq=%22fundamental+theorems%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwi9ura8y7vXAhWBnJQKHWdTCsgQ6AEI0AEwIA#v=onepage&q=%22fundamental%20theorems%22&f=false|page=114
|passage=There are two fundamental theorems of calculus. Both relate differentiation to integration. In most calculus courses, the Second Fundamental Theorem is usually proved first and then used to prove the First Fundamental Theorem. Unfortunately, this results in a First Fundamental Theorem that is '''weaker''' than it could be.}}
# Lacking in vigour or expression.
#: {{ux|en|a '''weak''' sentence; a '''weak''' style}}
# Not prevalent or effective, or not felt to be prevalent; not potent; feeble.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Midsummer|act=III|scene=ii|passage=Thy threats have no more strength than her '''weak''' prayers.}}
# {{lb|en|stock market}} Tending towards lower prices.
#: {{ux|en|a '''weak''' market; wheat is '''weak''' at present}}
# {{lb|en|photography}} Lacking [[contrast]].
#: {{ux|en|a '''weak''' negative}}
